summary: John's 10th-great-grandfather; Southold founder, lawyer, first High Sheriff of Yorkshire (Long Island) and member of Gov. Nicolls's council.
bio: Tombstone gives age 63 at death on 13 Nov 1671 (so born c.1608); tradition 'a native of Norwich, born 1608'. Hayes says he 'is said to have come from England June 19, 1635' with John Baylis; a 'William Wells, 17' on the Truelove in 1635 does not fit his age or legal training; a Richard Wells on the Globe 'for Virginia' 1635 is a different man (settled Salisbury, Mass.). At Southampton, 15 Mar 1643, 'William Wells, Gent., was censured for some unreverent speeches' to Daniel Howe. Southold's leading founder after Rev. John Youngs; its lawyer; council member; first High Sheriff of Yorkshire (the colonial county of Long Island, Staten Island and Westchester), 1664; sat on Gov. Nicolls's five-member council in 1664; justice of the peace; helped draft the Duke's Laws. Married (1) about 1650 Bridget, widow of Henry Tuthill, becoming guardian of her Tuthill children; (2) about 1654 Mary (surname unknown), mother of Mehitable (b. 1666). His will of 13 Nov 1671 left everything to 'my well beloved wife Mary Wells'. His tombstone in the old Southold burying ground was described by Pelletreau as possibly 'the oldest tombstone in Suffolk county'. TREE: parents 'Rev. William Wells to the Queen of Denmark' (1566–1620) and 'ANNE ELIZABETH Hunt Kimball ^ Welles, of St Albans, Immigrant' (1568–1646) — the prebendary's son William (bapt. 10 Feb 1604/5) became vicar of North Elmham and died in England in 1680, so this is disproven (Round 3); the mother is unsupported. Society of Colonial Wars: qualifies easily (council member, JP, sheriff) — the best colonial route, which also bypasses the James/Joshua confusion. Cousins via Wells: Anna Symmes Harrison (5C6R), Benjamin Harrison (7C4R).
notable: First High Sheriff of Yorkshire (Long Island), 1664; Gov. Nicolls's council; helped draft the Duke's Laws.
funFacts: His gravestone may be the oldest in Suffolk County.
